subsystems.name: Chassis and propulsion
subsystems.role: carries the device to the wound and moves it across the damaged surface.

subsystems.name: Targeting and sensing
subsystems.role: recognises damaged tissue while ignoring healthy skin.

subsystems.name: Actuation and payload
subsystems.role: delivers chemical or physical signals that help close the wound.

subsystems.name: Control and imaging
subsystems.role: external system tracks the devices and sends commands.

subsystems.name: Clearance
subsystems.role: breaks down safely once repair is under way.

buildSteps.title: Design the chassis
buildSteps.detail: Choose materials that are biocompatible, resorbable and rigid enough to carry a payload; model shapes at roughly 10–100 micrometres.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate at micro- and nanoscale
buildSteps.detail: Use two-photon lithography, microfluidics or DNA origami to build bodies and moving parts with nanometre precision.

buildSteps.title: Add propulsion
buildSteps.detail: Deposit magnetic layers for magnetic steering, or shape the body asymmetrically so it responds to ultrasound.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise the surface
buildSteps.detail: Attach ligands that bind to exposed collagen or fibrin at a wound, so the devices accumulate there.

buildSteps.title: Load the payload
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate growth factors, enzymes or crosslinkers in compartments that release only when a trigger is detected.

buildSteps.title: Test in skin models
buildSteps.detail: Apply to cultured keratinocytes and fibroblasts, and to lab-grown skin equivalents, to measure closure and toxicity.

buildSteps.title: Animal studies
buildSteps.detail: Test in small and large animal wound models for safety, immune response and healing speed.

buildSteps.title: Clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: First test for safety in small wounds, then compare efficacy against standard dressings.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and regulate
buildSteps.detail: Scale up sterile production and agree with regulators how such an active device should be classified and approved.

prerequisites.tech: Micro/nanorobotic propulsion and control in vivo
prerequisites.why: magnetically steered particles have been moved through animal tissue, but not yet with the precision needed for cell-level repair.
polymers and lipids are already used in resorbable implants and drug carriers.
DNA nanomachines and molecular motors work in a test tube; operating reliably inside living tissue is much harder.
advanced microscopy and ultrasound can track large particles, but not swarms of nanoscale robots deep in tissue.
liposomes and polymer nanoparticles already deliver drugs to specific tissues, showing the principle of localised therapy.

pathway.milestone: researchers steer magnetic microrobots and nanoparticles to wounds in animals, mainly to deliver drugs.
pathway.unlocks: proof that tiny devices can reach a wound and stay there.

pathway.milestone: microrobots that both sense a wound and release healing factors on demand.
pathway.unlocks: faster closure in animal models compared with passive dressings.

pathway.milestone: swarms that physically pull cell edges together while delivering factors.
pathway.unlocks: a device that can help close a wound without sutures.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous, resorbable nanobot patches for human use.
pathway.unlocks: rapid repair of burns, surgical incisions and chronic ulcers — if safety and control are proven.
